requests.request_text: DEFINITIONS   WRITING means all writings as defined by Evidence Code Section 250 including all written, recorded or graphic matters, however produced or reproduced, whether or not privileged, including, but not limited to, any and all originals, copies or drafts of any and all of the following:letters, correspondence, telegrams, telexes or cables prepared, drafted, received or sent; memoranda, records, minutes, files, or diaries; tapes, transcripts or recordings; photostatings, photographs, pictures or films, including microfilm, microfiche, x‑rays and videotape; notes, summaries, reports, forecasts or appraisals; memoranda or records of telephone or in-person conversations by or with any person; office or inter-office communications; contracts, agreements, estimates, or bids; drawings, sketches, diagrams or blueprints; schedules, orders or acknowledgements; invoices, receipts or checks; bulletins, circulars, pamphlets, manuals or advertising brochures, studies, analyses, charts, indices, logs or reports; accounting records or work sheets; computer programs, computer data, electronically stored or computerized information, or electronic mail; any other graphic, symbolic, recorded or written materials of any nature whatsoever. Any writing that contains any comment, notation, addition, insertion or marking of any kind that is not part of another document, or any document that does not contain any comment, notation, addition, insertion or marking of any kind that is a party of another document, is to be considered as a separate document. Kier Associates has a long and highly successful history of providing environmental
science support services to state and federal agencies, Native Tribes,
environmental nonprofit organizations, and private wildland managers.   
  In 2012-13, Kier Associates conducted cost surveys of randomly selected California
cities to produce the report, Waste in Our Water: The Annual Cost to
California Communities of Reducing Litter That Pollutes Our Waterways, to
provide the public with an understanding of the costs of litter abatement to
taxpayer funded jurisdictions in California.    Now, the California Office of the Attorney General has asked our team to update this
research for the purpose of producing a new report with current cost
information.  That request is the reason that we are asking for your
cooperation in providing us with the cost information requested in the attached
survey.  We will use the information your jurisdiction provides to produce
an updated Annual Cost to California Communities report. For
your information, we attach the original 2013 report here, so you can further
understand the purpose of our inquiry.   

It’s our hope that the numbers can be simply lifted directly from your
line-item budget, inserted in the appropriate spaces in the attached survey,
and returned to us.  However, should this prove not possible, we do
appreciate your assistance in interpreting that budget and providing the data
requested.  
Please provide the requested information no later than Friday, April 12.   
If you have questions or would prefer to complete this survey by telephone, please
contact Barbara Stickel at 805-801-2663, or reducedebris@outlook.com.  
Thank you for your assistance.

SF Treasurer,   Under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552), I am requesting access to records or information regarding the backlog and processing times of Property Tax assessment appeals within Treasurer & Tax Collector, City and County of San Francisco.  Specifically, I am interested in obtaining information on the following:   The current number of Property Tax assessment appeals that are pending review.  Detailed reasons for the backlog in processing these appeals, if any.  The average time taken to process an appeal from the time of its filing.  Any measures being implemented or planned to address and reduce the backlog.  Correspondence and memos related to the processing delays of Property Tax assessment appeals.   I believe that the requested information is within your agency's jurisdiction and would not require an unreasonable amount of time to locate and produce the records.  Please include all relevant records from the past year, regardless of format, medium, or physical characteristics. If certain parts of the requested documents are exempt from disclosure by law, I request that you provide me with the non-exempt portions of the documents.  I am seeking these documents as part of research into public interest concerns regarding the efficiency and responsiveness of public services related to property tax administration. I would appreciate your consideration of a waiver or reduction of fees associated with this request given its contribution to the public understanding of government operations and activities.  If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $20. However, I would also request that you waive any fees, as this information is not being sought for commercial purposes but rather as part of a public interest inquiry.  I look forward to your response within the statutory time frame of 20 business days, as outlined by the FOIA.  Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Code Chapter 67) and the California Public Records Act, I request the following records. This is not an Immediate Disclosure Request.   The daily calendar kept under Admin. Code §67.29-5 for each person who served as head of the Department of Public Health, including acting or interim heads, from January 1, 2018 through the date of your search. Please include every entry concerning City business (meetings, calls, events, travel and blocked time), including entries that were later cancelled, declined or rescheduled. Rolling production. Please release records on a rolling basis, starting with the most recent 24 months and then working back one calendar year at a time. Redactions. I am not requesting purely personal entries excluded by §67.29-5, and I have no objection to redacting private individuals' personal contact information. Hello SF Department of Public Health,   My name is Robert Byrd, and I’m an officer of the local non-profit organization Pro-Life San Francisco. I am submitting a brand new request for public records under the California Public Records Act and the SF Sunshine Ordinance concerning Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital (“General Hospital”).   Previously, I have been able to retrieve records about General Hospital directly from the information officers at the University of California San Francisco (“UCSF”), as it is one of their teaching hospitals. But they recently informed me that, going forward, any information concerning General Hospital should be retrieved through the SF Department of Public Health (“DPH”). Please refer to PRA 025-023: “For any portion of the records requests regarding information related to Zuckerberg San Francisco General, please contact https://www.sf.gov/get-public-records-dph to submit a request for responsive records.”   I respectfully request to inspect public records, for the following:   Request No. 1  Memorandums, e-mails, texts, or other communications in the possession or control of General Hospital and the ZSFG Women's Options Center (6G), its administrators, staff, or volunteers, regarding contractual relationships, acquisitions, shipments, and correspondence with the companies Advanced Bioscience Resources Inc. and Cercle Allocation Services Inc. The time period for this request is from January 1, 2022 to the present date.   Request No. 2  The standardized “abortion Pregnancy Consultation and Evaluation” form, which is mentioned in a medical staff report on the SF.Gov website under the section titled Protocol #15: Procedure: Pre-operative Evaluation for Second Trimester Abortion” (PDF pages 126-130):  https://www.sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-12/DEC%202023%20JCC%20OPEN%20SESSION_FINAL%2012.12.23.cleaned.pdf#page=129   Please advise whether blank versions of this form are available. If not, I request that DPH redact any personally identifiable information from the record before transmitting the responsive documents. If this form has gone through language updates/changes, each version should be considered a separate responsive document. The time period for this request is from January 1, 2015 to the present date.   Request No. 3  Memorandums, e-mails, texts, invoices, handwritten documents, or other communications in the possession or control of General Hospital and the ZSFG Women's Options Center (6G) regarding the collection and transportation of fetal tissue from elective abortions. One such type of record previously provided to my organization under PRA 020-107 was called a “Tissue Log.” Email threads were also provided, from when the pandemic affected the record keeping process.    To assist in a records search, responsive records may mention, or include communications with, the UCSF Human Research Protection Program and UCSF Supply Chain Management. The time period for this request is from July 1, 2021 to the present date.   Request No. 4  Also in connection with Protocol #15 mentioned above, any facility or staff communications, emails, or other documents concerning the timing of when to give General Hospital patients the “Consent for Tissue Donation” form (which was previously provided to my organization under PRA 020-107).   If there is any confusion about the word “timing,” the question I seek an answer to is whether the Tissue Donation form is contained within an initial packet of intake documents during a patient’s first visit, or provided separately at a later time. If a responsive document has any sensitive information whatsoever, we ask that DPH redact that portion of the record and deliver to us the remainder of the responsive document. The time period for this request is from January 1, 2015 to the present date.    REQUEST FOR INFORMATION IN ELECTRONIC FORMAT PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 6253.9 (A) (2) & (E)   I am seeking these records in any and all electronic formats your office keeps them in. Under the Public Records Act, you are required to deliver the information in whatever electronic format it is in no matter whether it is Excel, Word, WordPerfect or some other program or programs. Government Code section 6253.9 (a) (2) & (e). My request extends to receipt of this information in the electronic format your office maintains these records in. Delivery of this information to me by electronic mail (Robert Byrd (robert@prolifesf.com)) or via a thumb drive or via a disk is fine. I can supply your agency with a thumb drive if needed. Please advise what electronic format these records are kept in.   In addition, if there are documents that satisfy this request that are in both electronic and paper formats, I offer to receive the electronic version of those records and forgo inspection and potential photocopying of those paper copies. It is hoped that this will save both your agency and me our time, trouble and expense.   If you anticipate that data compilation, extraction, or programming will be required to satisfy a request (per Section 6253.9(b)), please provide a written estimate and justification for the same.    REQUEST FOR INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS   For any records not delivered electronically, once I have had an opportunity to inspect these records, I will designate which documents I will wish to obtain copies from your office and its agents, employees, consultants, etc. If a document exists in both electronic and paper formats, I select to receive a copy of the electronic version of the document. This should save both your office time and funds in duplication time and costs and me duplication costs.   Also, on May 28, 2020 the California Supreme Court ruled that an agency may not charge a requestor of responsive documents for the act of searching for those documents or for review and redaction of any portion of a responsive document where the agency is claiming it is subject to an exemption or privilege. National Lawyers Guild v. City of Hayward, et al (2020) 9 Cal. 5th 488.   The California Public Records Act requires that responses be made within 10 days. Please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.   If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific statutory exemption you feel justifies the refusal to release the information and which official authorized the withholding of the responsive documents in whole or in part. Also, please provide all segregable portions of otherwise exempt material.    If you wish to discuss any of my requests for documents, please do not hesitate to contact me (Govt. Code section 6253.1).    Thank you for your cooperation, and I look forward to hearing from you soon.   All the best,  Robert Byrd  Executive Coordinator  Pro-Life San Francisco

Hi folks,   I hope you guys are doing well. I am working on a story checking in on the SoMa Rise center after it’s been operational for several months. I have a big list of questions, so let me know what things you can answer now and what you may need more time on. Many of these questions have multiple questions, so please answer each question individually. Here’s the list:   1. The center was originally 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. with a goal of going 24/7. Have you guys switched to operating 24/7? If so, what date did you begin operating 24/7? Have you ever had staffing issues that made operating 24/7 difficult or impossible? If the center hasn’t gone to 24/7 operations, why not?   2. The meth task force study said 4,000 people use meth in the city, and the center has about 20 beds. It started with 17 at first and then expanded to 20. Has the center expanded further? If so, how many beds are currently available for sobering? And if not, what are the hurdles preventing SoMa Rise from expanding and providing more beds?   3. Are people using meth nearby the center? In August, we found there were several encampments nearby and people using drugs only a block away from the center. Has open drug use outside the center been a problem? If not, how has SOMA Rise kept the area around the center clear of drugs?   4. How many times since opening has the center gone over capacity? How often does the center go over capacity? What happens when the center goes over capacity? What are some reasons the center may go over capacity?   5. In August SoMa Rise reported 315 visits. How many visits does the center get on average per day? Per month? How many visits total so far since opening? The center in August told the Chronicle it “counts visits, no unique guests, and can’t yet report how many are repeat visitors.” Has the center begun counting guests? How many repeat visitors are there? How many times have they come in? Is there a person or people who are frequent visitors? If so, how many times have they visited the center? Have there been any spikes in visitors since opening?   6. Guests who leave the center went to various locations when we reported on the center in August. At the time the #1 place the center took people was the Tenderloin Center. Since its closure, where are most people going after they leave the center? How many people go back to the street? How many people go to other centers, like St. Anthony’s? How many are going to shelters? How many to SF General? What are often the reasons for someone to go to SF General or another hospital?   7. Where are referrals coming from? Before it was the TL Center and the Street Crisis Response Team. Who refers the most people to the sobering center? What is the referral process like? How many are referrals and how many are walk-ins?   8. How many people ask about housing or inquire about housing placements at the center? Do you track how many people ask about housing? On average, how many people are asking about housing after going to the center?   9. We reported that people who visit the center usually stay about 4-8 hours. Is that still true?   10. Have any of the SOMA Rise guests been involved in any criminal activity in the area? Have you guys had to call SFPD ever at the center? If so, how many times? What are some of the reasons the center might call the police?   11. What are some learning lessons you’ve had since opening the center? Are there any bottlenecks in care that you guys have noticed? Have you guys changed anything about the approach that you did originally? Anything you guys have learned from the patients? Anything you guys have learned works/doesn’t work from operating the center for several months now?   Those are the bulk of my questions, please let me know when you guys could have answers for me on these. Like I said, please also let me know if anything is harder to get than other things.   Looking forward to hearing from you.   Best,   --   Adalberto “Aldo” Toledo  City Hall Reporter  San Francisco Chronicle  Cell: 281-235-4599

January 9, 2024  Madison Alvarado  Reporter, San Francisco Public Press   RE: Public Records Request   Dear San Francisco Department of Public Health,   My name is Madison Alvarado and I am a reporter with the San Francisco Public Press.    Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Government Code Section 6250 et seq.), I ask to obtain a copy of the following records:    All communications (including emails, text messages, and messages on platforms such as Twitter direct messages, Facebook messenger, Signal, WhatsApp, Slack, Gettr or Telegram, or any other messaging apps that the various) to or from DPH employees that are related to or which mention implementation of SB 43 for the following time period: Sent or received between December 1, 2023 and present day    I ask that you acknowledge receipt of this request once it is received, and ask for a determination on this request within 10 days of your receipt of it as required by the law, and an even faster reply if you can make that determination without having to review the record[s] in question. I also ask that you share the records on a rolling basis instead of waiting to collect everything and releasing all of the records at once.   Please note, the City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) case in which the California Supreme Court unanimously held the public has a right to see emails and text messages pertaining to public affairs that are sent from, or received on, government employees and officials personal devices and email accounts. A public record is still a public record no matter where it is kept, how it was transmitted or where it is retained.   This request reasonably describes identifiable records, and I believe there exists no express provision of law exempting such records from disclosure.    If you determine that any or all or the information qualifies for an exemption from disclosure, I ask you to note whether, as is normally the case under the Act, the exemption is discretionary, and if so whether it is necessary in this case to exercise your discretion to withhold the information. If you determine that some but not all of the information is exempt from disclosure and that you intend to withhold it, I ask that you redact it for the time being and make the rest available as requested. In any event, please provide a signed notification citing the legal authorities on which you rely if you determine that any or all of the information is exempt and will not be disclosed.   I would also ask that you waive copying fees if possible as this request is meant to serve the public. If you are unable to waive fees, please notify me of the total cost in advance of producing said documents.    If I can provide any other clarifications that will help expedite your attention to my request, please contact me at (925) 285-8645. Thank you for your time and attention.   Sincerely,  Madison Alvarado

I am certain of this because there is a lot of construction occurring on the bulbouts throughout Duboce Triangle, so I was extremely careful to park mid-block far away from any no-parking signs. I looked closely for any construction signs. There were none.   My car got ticketed and towed less than 72 hours later in the 10:00 am hour on Tuesday, January 30. In addition, I did not receive a text message from SFMTA prior to the towing even though I signed up for that service.   I checked the Duboce Triangle Facebook page to see if anyone else had a similar experience. Sure enough, a neighbor parked his car on the same block at 9:00 am on Monday, January 29. He said there were no posted signs. He returned to move his car 24 hours later on Tuesday, January 30 to find tow-away signs posted along the entire block and his car towed.   SFMTA and/or Public Works did not properly post the construction tow-away signs at least 72 hours in advance as required by law. I would like to find out what happened, why this happened, and if the company or person who improperly posted the signs lied about when they posted the signs.

According to a December 27th 2023 complaint filed by the New York Times (NYT), Microsoft and OpenAI generative artificial intelligence (“GENAI”) tools rely on large-language models (“LLMs”) that were built “by copying and using millions of NYT copyrighted news articles, in-depth investigations, opinion pieces, reviews, how-to guides and more. (…) Through Microsoft’s Bing Chat (recently rebranded as ‘Copilot’) and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, both Microsoft and OpenAI seek to free-ride on the NYT massive investment in its journalism by using it to build substitutive product without permission or payment. (…) At the same time as Microsoft and OpenAI models are copying, reproducing, and paraphrasing NYT content without consent or compensation, they are also causing the NYT commercial and competitive injury by misattributing content to the NYT that it did not, in fact, publish. In AI parlance, this is called a ‘hallucination.’ In plain English, it’s misinformation. ChatGPT defines a ’hallucination’ as the ‘phenomenon of a machine, such as a chatbot, generating seemingly realistic sensory experiences that do not correspond to any real-world input.’ Instead of saying, ‘I don’t know,’ Microsoft and OpenAI GPT models will confidently provide information that is, at best, not quite accurate, and, at worst, demonstrably (but not recognizably) false. And human reviewers find it very difficult to distinguish ‘hallucinations’ from truthful output. These ‘hallucinations’ mislead users as to the source of the information they are obtaining, leading them to incorrectly believe that the information provided has been vetted and published by the NYT. Users who ask a search engine what the NYT has written on a subject should be provided with neither an unauthorized copy nor an inaccurate forgery of a NYT article, but a link to the article itself.”       The NYT have also noted in their December 27th 2023 complaint that “it takes enormous resources to publish, on average, more than 250 original articles every day. Many of these articles take months – and sometimes longer – to report. That output is the work of approximately 5,800 full-time equivalent Times employees (as of December 31st 2022), some 2,600 of whom are directly involved in the Time’s journalism operation. Quite often, the most vital news reporting for society is the most resource-intensive. Some of The Time’s most important journalism requires deploying teams of journalists at great cost to report on the ground around the world, providing best-in-class-security and support, filing lawsuits against government entities to bring information to light, and supporting journalists through investigations that can take months or years. (…) Making great journalism is harder than ever. Over the past two decades, the traditional business models that supported quality journalism have collapsed, forcing the shuttering of newspapers all over the country. It has become more difficult for the public to sort fact from fiction in today’s information ecosystem, as misinformation floods the internet, television, and other media. If The Times and other news organizations cannot produce and protect their independent journalism, there will be a vacuum that no computer or artificial intelligence can fill. What are “impairments”?      Types of impairment that may in some individuals result in a disability include, but are not limited to: orthopedic, visual, speech, hearing impairments, tuberculosis, HIV and AIDS, muscular dystrophy, learning disabilities, diabetes, emotional and mental illness, multiple sclerosis, cancer, developmental disability, heart disease, cerebral palsy and epilepsy.       What are “major life activities”?      Includes activities such as: reading, speaking, breathing, standing, hearing, lifting, learning, sitting, performing manual tasks, walking, and caring for oneself. Additionally, working is considered a major life activity in the particular circumstances when the individual is unable to perform a broad range of jobs or a class of jobs because of his/her disability.       What does “substantially limits” mean?    “Substantially limits” means the individual either is unable to perform a major life activity that the average person in the general population can perform; or is restricted significantly as to the condition, manner or duration under which he/she can perform the activity as compared to the condition, manner or duration under which the average person in the general population can perform the activity.       Who is considered a “qualified individual with a disability?”      A “qualified individual with a disability” is an individual with a disability who meets the skill, experience, education, and other job-related of a position held or desired, and who, with or without reasonable accommodation, can perform the essential functions of such job. Persons who cannot perform the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation, or who do not meet the prerequisite qualifications for the job, or who pose a direct threat of a significant risk to health or safety that cannot be eliminated by reasonable accommodation, are not otherwise qualified and may be terminated/not hired, consistent with how persons without a disability are treated in similar circumstances.       What are “essential functions”?      Essential functions are the fundamental duties of a job that an employee must be able to perform (to the prevailing standard), with or without accommodation. Functions may be essential if:          They are the reason the position exists;  They require the possession of specific experience/skills;  They cannot be distributed or assigned to others;   All other employees similarly classified are required to perform them;  A significant amount of time is spent performing them;   The consequences of not performing them are considerable.      What is a “reasonable accommodation?”      An “accommodation” is a modification or adjustment to the hiring process, work environment, or manner in which work is performed customarily that enables a qualified individual with a disability to be considered to perform the essential functions of a position to the prevailing standards. The College is required to make reasonable accommodation for a qualified individual with a disability. Reasonable accommodations are determined on a case-by-case basis with the participation of the employee. An accommodation is reasonable when undertaking it would not cause the employer to incur undue hardship, when it is not requested for marginal job functions, or when the request is not for a personal item or service.    What are “marginal job functions?”      Marginal job functions are non-essential job functions. Although these may be reassigned to other persons as a job accommodation, the employer need not to do so.       The College is not required to make an accommodation if it would impose undue hardship on the operation of its programs. The concept of undue hardship includes any action that is unduly costly, extensive or disruptive. That is, the action requires significant difficulty or expense when considered in light of one or more of the following factors:     Nature and net cost of accommodations;   Number of employees and/or students;   Effect of expenses and resources;   Overall financial resources;   Impact upon operation of the institution or unit;  Impact upon academic requirements;   Number, type and location of facilities; and  Type operations of the employer, including the composition, structure and functions of the workforce, and the geographic separateness and administrative or fiscal relations of the facility/facilities in question to the College. What are “impairments”?      Types of impairment that may in some individuals result in a disability include, but are not limited to: orthopedic, visual, speech, hearing impairments, tuberculosis, HIV and AIDS, muscular dystrophy, learning disabilities, diabetes, emotional and mental illness, multiple sclerosis, cancer, developmental disability, heart disease, cerebral palsy and epilepsy.       What are “major life activities”?      Includes activities such as: reading, speaking, breathing, standing, hearing, lifting, learning, sitting, performing manual tasks, walking, and caring for oneself. Additionally, working is considered a major life activity in the particular circumstances when the individual is unable to perform a broad range of jobs or a class of jobs because of his/her disability.       What does “substantially limits” mean?    “Substantially limits” means the individual either is unable to perform a major life activity that the average person in the general population can perform; or is restricted significantly as to the condition, manner or duration under which he/she can perform the activity as compared to the condition, manner or duration under which the average person in the general population can perform the activity.       Who is considered a “qualified individual with a disability?”      A “qualified individual with a disability” is an individual with a disability who meets the skill, experience, education, and other job-related of a position held or desired, and who, with or without reasonable accommodation, can perform the essential functions of such job. Persons who cannot perform the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation, or who do not meet the prerequisite qualifications for the job, or who pose a direct threat of a significant risk to health or safety that cannot be eliminated by reasonable accommodation, are not otherwise qualified and may be terminated/not hired, consistent with how persons without a disability are treated in similar circumstances.       What are “essential functions”?      Essential functions are the fundamental duties of a job that an employee must be able to perform (to the prevailing standard), with or without accommodation. Functions may be essential if:          They are the reason the position exists;  They require the possession of specific experience/skills;  They cannot be distributed or assigned to others;   All other employees similarly classified are required to perform them;  A significant amount of time is spent performing them;   The consequences of not performing them are considerable.      What is a “reasonable accommodation?”      An “accommodation” is a modification or adjustment to the hiring process, work environment, or manner in which work is performed customarily that enables a qualified individual with a disability to be considered to perform the essential functions of a position to the prevailing standards. The College is required to make reasonable accommodation for a qualified individual with a disability. Reasonable accommodations are determined on a case-by-case basis with the participation of the employee. An accommodation is reasonable when undertaking it would not cause the employer to incur undue hardship, when it is not requested for marginal job functions, or when the request is not for a personal item or service.    What are “marginal job functions?”      Marginal job functions are non-essential job functions. Although these may be reassigned to other persons as a job accommodation, the employer need not to do so.       The College is not required to make an accommodation if it would impose undue hardship on the operation of its programs. The concept of undue hardship includes any action that is unduly costly, extensive or disruptive. That is, the action requires significant difficulty or expense when considered in light of one or more of the following factors:     Nature and net cost of accommodations;   Number of employees and/or students;   Effect of expenses and resources;   Overall financial resources;   Impact upon operation of the institution or unit;  Impact upon academic requirements;   Number, type and location of facilities; and  Type operations of the employer, including the composition, structure and functions of the workforce, and the geographic separateness and administrative or fiscal relations of the facility/facilities in question to the College. The plaintiff can create rebuttable presumption of negligence by proving that the harm would not ordinarily have occurred without the negligence of the defendant, that the object that caused the harm was under the defendant’s control, and that there are no other plausible explanations.   To prove res ipsa loquitur negligence, the plaintiff must prove 3 things:     The incident was of a type that does not generally happen without negligence  It was caused by an instrumentality solely in defendant’s control  The plaintiff did not contribute to the cause    “Res ipsa loquitur.” Cornell Law School. https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/res_ipsa_loquitur .      For res ipsa loquitur to apply, the accident in question must not be due to any voluntary action or contribution by the plaintiff. The doctrine has traditionally required that a defendant have exclusive control over the instrumentality of an injury, but now it is commonly applied when multiple defendants have joint or sometimes successive control (as by the manufacturer and retailer of a defective product). In addition to the control requirement, and sometimes superseding it, is the requirement that a defendant have responsibility for the instrumentality as well as responsibility to the plaintiff. In order for res ipsa loquitur to succeed in a medical malpractice suit, the fact that the accident is one that ordinarily does not occur without a failyre to exercise due care must be readily apparent to the layperson as common knowledge. The accident alone should afford reasonable evidence of negligence, as when a foreign object is left inside a surgical patient. “Res ipsa loquitur.” Merriam-Webster.com Legal Dictionary, Merriam-Webster. https://www.merriam-webster.com/legal/res%20ipsa%20loquitur . Hi Travis,   	Please see responses to your questions below in blue. If you’d like to attribute in your story, please attribute to The Controller Office.     Can you help me understand what specific steps PRC and Baker Places, Inc. took that allowed its status to change from red flag to elevated concern?   PRC/Baker Places developed and finalized its required sustainability plan, which included programmatic restructuring and cost-reducing measures to stabilize its financial position. Funding departments continued to work closely with PRC/Baker to monitor its progress in making longer term changes. The FY22-23 fiscal monitoring review found the agency to have significantly improved on its financial indicators compared to prior year losses, and that the agency has taken steps necessary to start moving in the right direction towards demonstrating financial stability. The Controller’s Office and funding departments has placed PRC/Baker on elevated concern to continue closely monitoring the agency’s progress in meeting the milestones per its sustainability plan and whether PRC/Baker continues to improve is financial position to meet the City’s financial and administrative standards.     And for the 257 line items in the data categorized as not yet in conformance, are there any consequences for the 46 organizations that failed to conform? And are there future deadlines to come into compliance?   When nonprofits don’t meet these fiscal and compliance standards, there are a variety of responses the City can take, which are guided by the citywide corrective action policy. Funding departments can require and hold meetings with the nonprofit’s leadership to make progress on required corrective actions. The City may provide technical assistance, where appropriate, to support the nonprofit to become compliant on fiscal/compliance standards. The City may also designate a nonprofit on elevated concern or red flag status for nonprofits who don’t meet specific standards over a period of time (e.g., repeated findings on the same standard for two years in a row). In each annual fiscal monitoring, City monitors review prior year findings to assess whether the nonprofit has resolved those issues, or if there is continued non-conformance which prompt the responses above.      Also, was a 2023 report following up on the Aug. 30, 2022, Citywide Nonprofit Performance Audit released by the controller?   The Controller’s Office issues a report every year on the results of the fiscal and compliance monitoring process. This work is not directly tied to the one-time audit published in 2022 on programmatic monitoring practices. However, as noted in the press release, the Controller’s Office is implementing additional initiatives to set new policy about programmatic monitoring, in part as a result of the 2022 audit report. While a contractor’s programmatic and financial performance are often related, the current fiscal and compliance monitoring annual report focuses on financial indicators.  Of those referrals, how many people received jail behavioral health services for substance use disorders;    The number of reports of substance use treatment recommendations filed in Superior Court;  The number of booked individuals who reported opioid use for withdrawal;  The number of prescriptions issued for medically supported withdrawal and/or medications for addiction treatment for booked individuals broken down by name of medication;  Total reimbursements for medications for addiction treatment through CalAIM;  The number of individuals incarcerated in San Francisco County Jail for more than three days who participated in alcoholics anonymous and/or narcotics anonymous programming while incarcerated and the average number hours individuals spent in either or both of the programs;  The number of referrals to community treatment through the Reentry Services program at time of discharge for people incarcerated for more than three days;   Of those referrals, how many individuals were placed in a community treatment program;    The percentage of formerly incarcerated people who attended a community follow up appointment and/or continued to receive medication for addiction treatment or opioid use disorder within 30 days of release.    If you believe any part of any of the documents requested is non-public please redact the information you believe to be non-public and provide the rest of the document or any summary information available. In the FY ending in 2021, “Reinvestment Initiatives” are labeled with code: 10036606. You can view the budget line on page 206 of the ordinance PDF here: https://sfcontroller.org/sites/default/files/Documents/Budget/AAO%20FY2020-21%20%26%20FY2021-22%20-%20FINAL.pdf. The relevant line is on page 188 of the 2023 budget: https://www.sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-08/Budget-and-AAO-FY2022-23-and-FY2023-24.pdf  The relevant line is on page 181 of the 2024 budget: https://www.sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-08/Budget-and-AAO-FY2023-24-and-FY2024-25.pdf  If you are having a hard time identifying what specific budget lines I’m looking at please let me know and I can provide additional details. San Francisco Controller’s Office  Public Records Unit   Hello,   This e-mail is a request for access to materials in possession of your department, the purpose of inspection and copying pursuant to my rights under the California Public Records Act, section 6250 of the Government Code. The information I want to inspect and copy is described as follows:      A dataset of San Francisco Sheriff’s office earnings for 2024, 2023 and 2022.  Data should include the officers’ first name, last name, job code, job title, date of hours worked, category of hours worked, number hours worked on that specific date, and the amount earned by those hours. For instance, 12:00 p.m.- 4p.m.      This request reasonably describes an identifiable record, and I believe there exists no express provision of law exempting such records from disclosure. Therefore, pursuant to state Government Code section 6257, I ask that you make the record "immediately available'' in electronic format or based on my payment of fees covering direct cost of duplication.   To the extent that a portion of the information I have requested is not immediately available, I request that whatever documentation is immediately available be turned over first.   To the extent that a portion of the information I have requested is exempt by express provision of law, the state Government Code section 6257 additionally requires that such material be redacted in order that the remainder of the information may be provided to satisfy my request.   In any case, if you determine that an express provision of law exists to exempt from disclosure all or a portion of the material I have requested, Government Code section 6256 requires a determination and notification to me of the reasons therefore no later than 10 days from your receipt of this request. Government Code Section 6256.2 prohibits the use of the 10-day period, or any other provision of the Public Records Act, ""to delay access for purposes of inspecting public records.''   Thank you for your timely attention to my request. I can be reached by telephone at 415-609-8677.   Yours truly,   Megan Cassidy

To whom it may concern :   My name is Shalah Lising Romine. My sister was found dead on January 14, 2022. My youngest nephew, her youngest son, was only 20 years old at the time of her death. We were both shocked and devastated, but because of his age he needed help to deal with the logistics of dealing with this overwhelming situation.    Thus, we agreed to share the responsibility of being next of kin. She was laying in the morgue for what felt like an eternity. One of the most painful experience that we shared was that we were both abandoned by our father. He did his best and was a loving man , but he did disappear on us for several years. We both were blessed to reconnect with him eventually and forgave him together. When he passed away on 4/8/2017, we had each other to grieve his death.    When I learned of her death, I couldn’t abandon her. I asked the Medical Examiner’s office if I could see her,  unfortunately I was denied due to the state of decomposition she was found.    I reached out to the Medical Examiner’s office about her autopsy in May of 2022. They advised me that it would be 8-10 months. I asked , from now? They advised that yes , from May of 2022. I finally received the autopsy February of 2024. The information included in the autopsy and accompanying documents was shocking to our family.    It was also quite surprising that the following discrepancies and delays occurred:   1) MEDICAL EXAMINER/INVESTIGATOR’S REPORT   CASE #: 2022-0048 Investigator J. Wil Chuakay #120 and Investigator Anthony Marchini #131 collective findings documented that her apartment was “sparsely furnished”. Not sure what happened to all of her things. Secondly, 2 glass pipes found - no mention of what kind of residue. 2 spoons tossed in the bed where she was found , but not collected as evidence.    2) FORENSIC LABORATORY DIVISION provided the REPORT OF FORENSIC TOXICOLOGY ANALYSES bore submission date and time on 01/18/2022 0730 hrs - Date of Report bears the date 04/01/2022 ; Case Reviewed by Jessica N. Winborn, PH.D signed and dated on April 04, 2022; Divisional Reviewed by Luke N. Rodda, PHD. MRACI CChem signed and dated April 20, 2022. When considering the amount of time that lapsed, and the half-life of many of the chemicals found in her system, and the kind of chemicals I am confused of how it possible for her to allegedly ingest all of these , yet absolutely no medication, no alcohol, and no tobacco. She was a smoker of cigarettes and cannabis.    There is no clarification of who provided her Medical History. “significant for alcohol use , depression, and psychotic disorder”. What psychotic disorder? It really makes no sense from my perspective.    3) MEDICAL EXAMINER/INVESTIGATOR’S REPORT   No Physician present.   Tech M. Conley  “Evidence: Blood Spot” no follow up.   Digitally Signed by Assistant ME -Jia Jun Guan on 04/29/2022. …. That would have been my sister’s 50th birthday.    I was provided the autopsy and accompanying reports February 2024, why did it take this long? As I mentioned, I called the ME in May of 2022.     Zacklyn, my niece, Ana May’s daughter, did ask for a copy. I emailed her a copy and called her so that I was able to FaceTime her to read through it with her. She is going to med school in the Philippines. It was one of the most difficult things I have ever had to do. Breaking my beautiful niece’s heart all over again. I pray for God’s forgiveness for this act that feels like a sin.    We are seeking as much information that we can so we can get to the truth. She is wanting the truth. I hope to bring her solace and get to begin the grieving process. Right now, there are too many questions. I know that utilizing FOIA will help fill in some blanks. My FOIA request is the first step.    Any help you can offer would be greatly helpful to my sister’s soul, me and my family.    In accordance with FOIA and my right as next of kin, I kindly would like to request the following:   * all toxicology notes taken by forensic toxicologist, and all notes from the Chief forensic toxicologist and director of the forensic laboratory division from the office of the chief medical examiner, in the city and county of San Francisco.  * contact information for investigator Jay Wil Chuakay#120 and investigator Anthony Martini, # 131.  * contact information from Bazen 58 from San Francisco fire department and Shah #2065 from San Francisco police department.   * Police report SFPD # : 220–0 27–272  * copies of the two anterior posterior total body radiographs  * contact information from the assistant, medical examiner, Jia June Guan, MD. I am in contact with Kristopher Zehn Lising, my youngest nephew.    Thank you for your time. I look forward to your response.   Shalah Romine  (904)6511306

Of particular interest are the following items:  •	Records regarding petroleum product and/or hazardous substance usage/storage at the subject property (i.e., permits, inspections, hazardous materials business plans, SPCC plans, maps, site plans, chemical inventories);  •	Records regarding aboveground storage tank (AST) and/or underground storage tank (UST) systems at the subject property;  •	Records of hazardous substance and/or petroleum product releases, contamination or other known environmental concerns which may have affected the subject property;  •	Records of violations or corrective actions;  •	Records of septic system installations and repairs at the subject property;   •	Records of wells in connection with the subject property; and/or  •	Environmental permits (wastewater discharges and/or air emissions) and the most recent associated effluent/emission sampling.  The time frame for this request is 1940-2024.  Thank you.

To whom it may concern,    I have a VERY old rusty fire escape on the back of my 1910 home that I would like to remove. I've lived here since 1988.  From researching this, my understanding is:  Since only two floors of my home are finished living space and there is a stairwell in between the first and second floor, I actually don't need this fire escape.  The fire escape can be accessed by the third floor attic space which is a non-livable/living space without finished walls, electricity or plumbing.  I've been advised to look at the permit history of my home to determine why the fire escape was built to reach the attic level of the house before removing the fire escape.    Please advise me on how to do this since there are no records online of permits prior to the 1980's. Many thanks in advance for your time.

requests.request_text: Hello: I am requesting the following information related to San Francisco’s food inspection program.    How many permitted retail food facilities were there in San Francisco in each of the following years: 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023?  How many permitted retail food facilities in San Francisco received at least one routine food inspection in each of the following years: 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023?  How many permitted retail food facilities in San Francisco received no routine food inspection in each of the following years: 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023?  How many reports of foodborne illness did DPH receive related to food facilities in San Francisco in each of the following years: 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023?  What is the department’s target response time to reports of foodborne illness? Of reports in those years, how many were responded to within the stated target?  How many food inspectors does San Francisco currently employ? How long have there been 10 vacant food inspector positions?

requests.request_text: I am writing regarding the Channel Pump station project on Berry street in Mission bay. I live directly next door at 355 Berry and have noticed a strong off gassing /chemical smell coming from the pump station, which is currently undergoing a multi year maintenance project.   My family has been experiencing burning nose, eyes, mouth, dizziness and breathing difficulties, specifically at times when the smell is observed.    We have been requesting info for over 6 months with no result. I would like to have more transparent information and data regarding how the safety of the plant and project are being monitored for environmental and human safety risks.    I am particularly concerned about offgassing of hydrogen sulfide, which has symptoms consistent with the symptoms my family and pets are experiencing.    I am now taking the next step is to request all public records regarding the project and associated water, air , chemical monitoring for the plant.

requests.request_text: Hello,   I’m looking for any records related to permits or approvals to run a dog kennel, pet hotel, or any type of animal boarding facility at 381 Duncan Street #A, San Francisco, CA 94131. Specifically, I’d love your help finding:    Any health permits, applications, renewals, approvals/denials, or status records for kennel or animal boarding operations at that address.  Any inspection reports or enforcement actions related to that kind of use.  Any zoning referral forms or Fire Marshal sign-offs connected to a kennel or boarding permit there.  And if no such records exist, just a note letting me know there’s nothing on file.    For reference, the business name might be Noe Dogwalkers, and the owner’s name is Lara Monroe. The business has been active since around July 2011.   Thanks so much for your time and help with this request!   Best,  Klevis Xharda

I am a writer-at-large at the New York Times Magazine and I am writing a story about San Francisco County’s response to COVID-19, specifically as it pertains to nursing homes, which should be defined as any Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) or Assisted Living Facility (ALF) in the state of California. As this request concerns a newsworthy and time sensitive topic of the utmost importance to the public, I ask that you respond expeditiously.  
   
 I am requesting access to records in possession or control of San Francisco County for the purposes of inspection and copying pursuant to the California Public Records Act, California Government Code § 6250 et seq. (“CPRA”), and Article I, § 3(b) of the California Constitution. The specific records I seek to inspect and copy are the following: 
 1) All records from November 1 2019 up until the current day that either detail, discuss or mention nursing homes with regards to COVID-19. This request includes a request for documents related to communications with other governmental agencies, such as internal communications with other county agencies and/or external communications with other municipalities, states, the Governor of California’s office, or the federal government. This request also includes a request for documents related to communications with any other entities or individuals, including but not limited to academics, scientists, public health professionals, hospital administrators, economists, pollsters. If there are any documents or memos that have circulated about the unique risk COVID-19 poses to nursing homes, please include those as well.  
 2) All records related to any discussion of testing capacities at nursing homes or any plans, memos our communication that discusses future plans to provide testing at nursing homes. This would include, but not only be limited to the order that was reported on May 6th by the San Francisco Chronicle that mandated testing in SNFs.  
 3) All records related to any discussions of nursing homes with regard to COVID-19, ESPECIALLY in late February and the entire month of March. If there was early guidance to nursing homes (SNFs or ALFs) for their response, we would appreciate the opportunity to look that over.  
 4) Any guidance, advice, declarations, communications or regulations from your office to nursing homes or companies that provide nursing home care. These would include mandates about who can enter and who can leave, testing regimens, care guidelines for COVID-19 positive residents. This would also include any declarations or guidance to place COVID-19 positive residents in nursing homes.  
 4) Any communications, including emails, letters, phone call audio, or the notes of any meetings with the owners, managers or regulators of nursing homes.  
 5) Any communications received from nursing home residents, their families, or any employees expressing concern or alarm regarding COVID-19 preparedness.  
 6) Any internal memos, messages or emails that assess the situation within nursing homes, whether data from other states, socioeconomic breakdowns or anything else related to COVID-19 and nursing homes. 
 7) The number of COVID-19 positive cases and deaths from COVID-19 that have taken place in nursing homes in San Francisco County. 
 As used herein, “Record” includes “Public Records” and “Writings” as those terms are defined at Government Code § 6252(e) & (g).  
 If you contend that any portion of the records requested is exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, Government Code § 6253(a) requires segregation and redaction of that material in order that the remainder of the records may be released. If you contend that any express provision of law exists to exempt from disclosure all or a portion of the records I have requested, Government Code § 6253(c) requires that you notify me of the reasons for the determination not later than 10 days from your receipt of this request. Government Code §§ 6253(d) & 6255(b) require that any response to this request that includes a determination that the request is denied, in whole or in part, must be in writing and include the name and title of the person(s) responsible for the County’s response.   
 Government Code § 6253(d) prohibits the use of the 10-day period, or any provisions of the CPRA or any other law, “to delay access for purposes of inspecting public records.” 
 In responding to this request, please keep in mind that Article 1, § 3(b)(2) of the California Constitution expressly requires you to broadly construe all provisions that further the public’s right of access, and to apply any limitations on access as narrowly as possible.     
 If I can provide any clarification that will help expedite your attention to my request, please contact me at jaycaspiankang@gmail.com, jay.kang@nytimes.com and please cc: sashabates20@gmail.com, pursuant to Government Code § 6253.1.  
   
 I ask that you notify me of any duplication costs exceeding $100 before you duplicate the records so that I may decide which records I want copied. 
 Thank you for your timely attention to this matter.  
 Sincerely, 
 Jay Caspian Kang 
 Writer at Large, New York Times Magazine

Of particular interest are the following items:  •	Records regarding petroleum product and/or hazardous substance usage/storage at the subject property (i.e., permits, inspections, hazardous materials business plans, SPCC plans, maps, site plans, chemical inventories);  •	Records regarding aboveground storage tank (AST) and/or underground storage tank (UST) systems at the subject property;  •	Records of hazardous substance and/or petroleum product releases, contamination or other known environmental concerns which may have affected the subject property;  •	Records of violations or corrective actions;  •	Records of septic system installations and repairs at the subject property;   •	Records of wells in connection with the subject property; and/or  •	Environmental permits (wastewater discharges and/or air emissions) and the most recent associated effluent/emission sampling.  The time frame for this request is 1920-2025.  Thank you.

requests.department_names: Public Health: Ground Water / Water Quality / Soil Borings
requests.request_text: I hope this message finds you well. My name is Lisa Anderson, and I’m a senior Environmental Engineering student at the University of San Francisco. My capstone partner, Amy Rios, and I are currently working on a project to design a smart buoy for real-time water quality monitoring in the water bodies of Golden Gate Park.  As part of our research, we are seeking any available documents, photos, emails, texts, videos, data, or other records that could help us better understand the water quality conditions in the park’s lakes and ponds. Specifically, we are interested in data on parameters like dissolved oxygen, pH, turbidity, temperature, and any other water quality metrics currently being measured in the park.  Any records or insights you can provide would greatly assist us in shaping the design and functionality of our monitoring system, ensuring it aligns with the park’s water quality management practices.  Please let us know if there are any materials available or if you can direct us to the appropriate sources. We’d be happy to meet with you to discuss this further, whether in person or virtually, at your convenience.

Sunshine Request and California Public Records Request   Please disclose any Controller's Office generated records that specifically address the SFPD's Sunshine Ordinance, Sunshine Ordinance records disclosure status within the last twenty-five (25) years. Please assist me in locating these records and please also feel free to contact me re fees or for clarity if needed.    Thank you,   Stacy Smith

IMMEDIATE DISCLOSURE REQUEST FOR PUBLIC RECORDS:  City Attorney Time and Expenses on Various LHH Legal Matters      August 8, 2024      David Chiu   City Attorney   San Francisco City Hall, Room 234   1 Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Place   San Francisco, California 94102-4682      Dear City Attorney Chiu,      This is an Immediate Disclosure Request for public records under San Francisco's Sunshine Ordinance, the California Public Records Act, Proposition 59, and the Brown Act.      The “Settlement and Systems Improvement Agreement” involving Laguna Honda Hospital and Rehabilitation Center (LHH) between (i) the City and County of San Francisco (“City”), acting by and through its Department of Public Health, which has administrative jurisdiction over and operates the Laguna Honda Hospital & Rehabilitation Center D/P SNF (“LHH”), (ii) the California Department of Public Health (“CDPH”), and (iii) the United States Department of Health & Human Services (“DHHS”), Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (“CMS”) (collectively, the “Parties”) was signed on November 12, 2022. The “Settlement Agreement” essentially ended in August 2023.      Page 4 of the “Settlement Agreement” stipulated that the agreement would expire or terminate when LHH obtained new Medicare or Medicaid provider agreement(s).      LHH received its MediCal (Medicaid) provider agreement on August 16, 2023, and its Medicare recertification provider agreement on June 20, 2024. Therefore, the “Settlement Agreement” should have expired on either Augst 16, 2023 (when in fact, the “Quality Improvement Expert” or “QIE” LHH had been required to hire stopped producing mandatory reports required by the “Settlement Agreement” to CMS, with the last “Monthly Monitoring Report” (#7) dated August 10, 2023, and the last “Root Cause Analysis Report” (#9) dated August 14, 2023. The end of production of those two types of reports signaled that the “Settlement Agreement” officially ended as of August 2023.      Therefore, for the purpose of this records request, please provide an Excel spreadsheet extracted from the CityLaw database software that tracks City Attorney billable time and expenses related to each of the following legal matters itemized by each matter:       LHH's potential closure and application to become re-certified with CMS;   LHH CEO Roland Pickens’ December 27, 2021 Informal Dispute Resolution appeal to the Licensing and Certification Program in the California Department of Public Health;  The three Administrative Law Judge appeals to the U.S. DHHS submitted by DCA Arnulfo Medina on behalf of City Attorney David Chiu;   Efforts to help the Board of Supervisors write two resolutions passed on July 26, 2022 — one to DHHS Secretary Xavier Becerra, and the other to Governor Newsom and Tomás Aragón;  On February 15, 2022, April 25, 2022 and May 28, 2022 LHH appealed the remedies included in the “Settlement and Systems Improvement Agreement,” by filing three appeals to the US DHHS Departmental Appeals Board (“DAB”), Civil Remedies Division (“CRD”).On June 2, 2022, the CRD consolidated all the cases under DAB Docket #  C-22-55.   On August 3, 2022 the City, LHH’s owner and operator, filed a Complaint against DHHS and Xavier Becerra, Secretary of DHHS, docketed in the United States District Court, Northern District of California, City and County of San Francisco v. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services et al., Case No. 3:22-CV-4500.  also on August 3, 2022, certain LHH residents, a resident conservator, and a resident guardian, filed a putative class action Complaint against Chiquita Brooks-LaSure, Administrator for CMS; Xavier Becerra, Secretary of DHHS; CDPH; and Tomás Aragón, Director of CDPH, docketed in the United States District Court, Northern District of California, D.B. et al. v. Brooks-LaSure et al., Case No. 3:22-CV-4501.   Preparation by Deputy City Attorneys for each of the multiple City contracts awarded to Health Management Associates (HMA) and to Health Services Advisory Group (HSAG) between May 2022 and today’s date.  Any other legal matters involving LHH’s potential closure, excluding any lawsuits filed on behalf of LHH’s residents.    Since many of these legal matters have clearly ended, there should be no reason the City Attorney’s time and expenses in the CityLaw database should remain open. IMMEDIATE DISCLOSURE REQUEST FOR PUBLIC RECORDS:  Pickens’ Follow-up to Supervisor Preston, and City Attorney Chiu’s August 3 Lawsuit       August 6, 2022      Grant Colfax   Director of Public Health   City and County of San Francisco   101 Grove Street   San Francisco, CA  94102      Roland Pickens    Acting Executive Administrator    Laguna Honda Hospital   375 Laguna Honda Boulevard    San Francisco, CA  94116       Grace Ye Chen    Clinical Nurse Specialist   Department of Public Health   City and County of San Francisco   101 Grove Street   San Francisco, CA  94102      Dear Dr. Colfax, Mr. Pickens, and Ms. Chen,      This is an Immediate Disclosure Request for Public Records under San Francisco’s Sunshine Ordinance, the California Public Records Act, Proposition 59, and the Brown Act.      This request seeks follow-up records regarding both the July 21 Board of Supervisors GAO hearing and City Attorney David Chiu’s August 3 District Court lawsuit regarding LHH.        1.      On July 21 GAO Chairperson Dean Peskin asked Mr. Pickens (at approximately 3:03:22 on videotape) about a slide Pickens had presented indicating that rather than the 18-month period LHH had requested to safely discharge all of LHH’s then 681 patients, CMS had said no, and had communicated a shorter timeline of just four months, until September 13 was required.       Supervisor Preston specifically asked Mr. Pickens what CMS had “communicated back and in writing” why CMS wanted such a short time period rather than 18 months. Preston followed up and asked Mr. Pickens to check whether there “was a letter or something where CMS laid out that the 18 months was too long and the reasons why.” Mr. Pickens said he would go back and check his records about what the dialog with CMS had been.        2.      City Attorney David Chiu’s August 3 Lawsuit Two paragraphs in the CAO’s August 3 District Court lawsuit are of interest:   Paragraph #41 Page 12 (Lines 25-28 and lines 1-5, page 13):“Per CMS, Laguna Honda is required to transfer or discharge all of its current patients within four months from the approval of the Closure Plan (approval of which is anticipated on May 13, 2022, with four months from that date being September 13, 2022), with a possible 2-month extension based on extenuating circumstances as approved by CDPH and CMS.”       Paragraph # 43, page 13, Lines 8-13): “Although federal regulations do not mandate that closure occur within any set period of time and allow the Secretary of HHS discretion to continue funding until the last patient is safely transferred or discharged from the facility, CMS and CDPH confirmed in several subsequent communications that federal funding will not be continued past September 13, 2022, and that all Medicare and Medicaid patients must be relocated by that date. This arbitrary and capricious decision constitutes an abuse of discretion.”    Please provide any records Mr. Pickens found in his records in response to Supervisor Preston’s request for what CMS had “communicated back and in writing” about why CMS wanted such a short time period rather than 18 months.      Please also provide any written records or meeting notes that supports the CAO’s assertion CMS required LHH to discharge all patients within four months by September 13, “confirmed (ostensibly in written records) in several subsequent communications,” indicating federal reimbursement would not continue past September 13.      Thank you.      Patrick Monette-Shaw   Columnist/Reporter   Westside Observer Newspaper   cc:       Public Records Staff, SFDPH              Alison Hawkes, DPH Director of Communications              Supervisor Dean Preston              Supervisor Connie Chan              Supervisor Raphael Mandelman              Supervisor Myrna Melgar

Dear Public Records Officer,   Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (CPRA), I respectfully request the following records from the San Francisco Department of Public Works (DPW):   1. Consultant Contracts (FY 2015–2025)  I request copies of all executed contracts that involve federal, state, or local funds for consultant services related to:   Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI)  Racial Equity  Gender Identity Policies  Environmental Justice   For each contract, please provide the following details:   Contract number and name of vendor/consultant  Total executed contract amount  A copy of the executed contract, including scope of work  Any contract amendments, modifications, or extensions, along with the associated dollar amounts  Funding source(s) (federal, state, local)    2. FTEs, Salaries, and Organizational Structure  I also request information regarding DPW employees working full-time and/or part-time on department-wide initiatives related to:   Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI)  Racial Equity  Gender Identity Policies  Environmental Justice  Participation in identity-based celebrations or observances, such as Black History Month, Women's History Month, Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month, Pride Month, etc.   For these positions, please provide:   The total number of FTEs assigned to the above initiatives  Position titles and job classifications  Annual salaries for each position  The office/division where each FTE is assigned  The most recent department-wide organization chart that breaks down the organization by division, bureau, and section, identifying the number of employees in each, broken down by Job Class    3. Racial Equity Action Plan & Working Group  The DPW website (Racial Equity Initiative) indicates that the department developed a Racial Equity Action Plan and established a Racial Equity Working Group. I request:   Copies of any contracts and subsequent modifications related to the development and implementation of the department’s Racial Equity Action Plan  A list of employees who participated in the Racial Equity Working Group, including:  Job class  Number of hours spent on developing and implementing the Racial Equity Action Plan      If any of the requested records are available in an electronic format, I prefer to receive them in that format to expedite review and analysis.   Sincerely,  DOGE SF

Public Records Act Request to the San Francisco Department of Public Works Custodian of the Records   November 13, 2024   Dear Custodian of the Records:   This request is a follow-up to my request of August 9, 2024, Record Request #24-4859, and your response of August 19, 2024, under the San Francisco Sunshine Ordinance, Chapter 67 of the San Francisco Administrative Code, the California Public Records Act, California Government Code sections 7920.000-7931.000, and Article I, section 3(b) of the California Constitution.   Specifically, I request any records in the possession or control of the Department of Public Works ("DPW") of the City and County of San Francisco, including any documents, photos, emails, texts, videos, data and all other records received or generated -- after August 19, 2024 to the present time -- regarding sidewalk defects at 1563-1565 Church St., San Francisco, California 94131 ("1563-1565 Church St."), as follows:    Any reports, including public complaints, relating to any sidewalk defects received by DPW, including, but not limited to, any lifted sidewalk defects at 1563-1565 Church St.  Any notices, including Notices to Repair, issued by DPW to the owner of the sidewalk at 1563-1565 Church St. to repair, remove, correct or modify any sidewalk defects, including, but not limited to, any lifted sidewalk defects.  Any action taken by the owner of the sidewalk at 1563-1565 Church St. to repair, remove, correct or modify any sidewalk defects, including, but not limited to, any lifted sidewalk defects. Applicable Legal Authority   The CPRA establishes a presumptive right of public access to records maintained by state and local agencies and provides that "every person has a right to inspect any public record" except as expressly exempted by law. Gov. Code § 6253(a). The CPRA requires that a determination regarding disclosable records be made within ten (10) calendar days of receipt of the request, with a possible fourteen (14) day extension under specified circumstances. Gov. Code § 6253(c).   The San Francisco Sunshine Ordinance further reinforces and expands upon these rights at the local level. Under the Sunshine Ordinance, public records must be made available for public inspection and copying "promptly" and no later than within ten (10) days of a request. S.F. Admin. Code § 67.21(b). The Sunshine Ordinance broadly defines "public records" to include "any writing containing information relating to the conduct of the public's business" that is "prepared, owned, used, or retained" by any city department. requests.department_names: Public Health: Hazardous Materials / USTs / Maher Ordinance
requests.request_text: Hello, I am requesting any information/documentation on file with the DPH regarding the Westfield San Francisco property (addresses ranging from 825-897 (all odd addresses) Market Street, 9-63 (all odd addresses) 5th Street; 376-398 (all even addresses) Mint Street; and 836-874 (all even addresses) Mission Street). Of particular interest are the following items:  •	Records regarding petroleum product and/or hazardous substance usage/storage at the subject property (i.e., permits, inspections, hazardous materials business plans, SPCC plans, maps, site plans, chemical inventories);  •	Records regarding aboveground storage tank (AST) and/or underground storage tank (UST) systems at the subject property;  •	Records of hazardous substance and/or petroleum product releases, contamination or other known environmental concerns which may have affected the subject property;  •	Records of violations or corrective actions;  •	Records of groundwater monitoring wells in connection with the subject property; and/or  •	Environmental permits (wastewater discharges and/or air emissions) and the most recent associated effluent/emission sampling.  The time frame for this request is 1940-2025. Thank you.

requests.request_text: Subject (copy and paste into subject field)  Public Records Act request for Operator Identification Numbers (OINs) and Restricted Permit Numbers   Body (copy and paste into body exactly as is, including brackets)  Commissioner {{Last name}},  Thank you for your assistance with my previous request. Due to the fact that some numbers were missing from the first responses, I am submitting a new, expanded request below.  Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, Cal. Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq. (formerly § 6250 et seq.), I respectfully request access to and copies of public records related to Operator Identification Numbers and Restricted Material Permit Numbers registered in San Francisco County. Specifically, I am requesting:   A list of all 2020 through 2025 Operator Identification Numbers (OINs) and Restricted Material Permit Numbers along with the name of the associated business or operator, and any public contact information and other publicly disclosable registration information associated with each operator.   If this data is maintained in a database, spreadsheet, or other structured digital format, I request it in its native electronic form (such as .xlsx, .csv, .txt, or a database export) pursuant to Gov. Code § 7922.570, which requires agencies to provide records in the format in which they are held when reasonably producible in that form.  I am not requesting any confidential information, proprietary data, or personal identifiers that are exempt under the PRA. If you believe any portion of a record is exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portion and cite the specific statutory exemption for each withheld or redacted portion, as required by § 7922.535.    Fees and Waiver  The Center for Investigative Reporting is a nonprofit newsroom, and disclosure of these records will contribute to the public’s understanding of government activities, not for commercial use. We therefore request that you waive any fees in accordance with the spirit of the PRA. If fees are unavoidable, please notify me in advance with an itemized estimate before processing.    Timing  As required by Gov. Code § 7922.535(a), I look forward to your determination within 10 days. If the records can be provided on a rolling basis, I welcome partial or interim releases to speed public access.    Delivery  Electronic delivery via email or secure file-transfer link is preferred. If you have questions that could help clarify or narrow the request, please feel free to contact me.  Thank you for your time and attention to this request, and I look forward to your response.  Sincerely,   David Ritsher  (415) 305-8457  dritsher@cir.org  www.cir.org  The Center for Investigative Reporting
