requests.request_text: “DBI” means the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection, including Housing Inspection Services (“HIS”), Building Inspection Division (“BID”), Code Enforcement Section/Division (“CES”), Code Enforcement Outreach Program (“CEOP”), Records Management, and any DBI employee or unit maintaining responsive records.  “VERITAS” means Veritas Investments, Inc., Greentree Property Management, Inc., RentSFNow, Yat-Pang Au/Yat Pang Au, and any address-specific ownership entity identified in DBI's own records as the owner, landlord, permit applicant, responsible party, property manager, agent or affiliated entity for a Schedule A Property. This definition is intended as a search aid and does not ask DBI to determine corporate affiliation.  “HRC/VTA” means Housing Rights Committee of San Francisco, Housing Rights Committee, HRC, Brad Hirn, Veritas Tenant Association, VTA, Veritas Tenants Campaign, and any successor or substantially similar designation reflected in DBI records.  “SCHEDULE A PROPERTIES” means the San Francisco addresses identified in Schedule A attached to this request, including properties involved in Evander v. Veritas Investments, Inc., McGlynn v. 634 Powell I5, LLC, and Stoops v. 300 Buchanan I3, LP. The request is address-based because responsive DBI records may identify address-specific LLCs or LPs rather than the name “Veritas.”  “SIMILAR CONDITIONS” means complaints, conditions, violations or investigations concerning construction or renovation in occupied residential buildings; construction of vacant units; work without permit; unsafe or disruptive construction; lack of construction notice; dust or debris; inadequate containment; lead or lead-paint disturbance; asbestos or asbestos disturbance; mold or microbial growth; moisture or water intrusion; plumbing leaks; water, gas, electricity or heat interruptions; elevator outages; damaged walls, ceilings, windows or floors; blocked or sealed windows; rodents, cockroaches, bedbugs or other pests; lack of heat; garbage or sanitation; reduction or loss of housing services; displacement or relocation connected with construction or repair; repeated or allegedly inadequate repairs; and other conditions substantially similar to the foregoing.  Unless a particular request provides otherwise, the “DETAILED RECORD PERIOD” is January 1, 2015 through December 31, 2022. For structured complaint/NOV data requested below, the period is January 1, 2008 through December 31, 2022 so that pre-acquisition and post-acquisition patterns can be evaluated.  Records Requested   Native building-complaint data. Produce the complete electronically maintained complaint data for every Schedule A Property from January 1, 2008 through December 31, 2022, including both complaints that resulted in an NOV and complaints that did not. Please include all existing fields reasonably associated with each complaint, including complaint number, property address, unit where maintained, block/lot, date received/filed, complaint source/category if maintained, assigned division, assigned inspector, complaint description, instructions, inspection date(s), status, status date, disposition, referral information, date closed, and complaint-status/comment/history fields. Tenant/complainant names, telephone numbers, email addresses and other personal identifying information may be redacted.  Native NOV data. Produce the complete electronically maintained Notice of Violation data for every Schedule A Property from January 1, 2008 through December 31, 2022, including complaint number, NOV number if separately maintained, date issued/filed, assigned division, code section/item violated, NOV category, inspector description/comments, address/unit, status, abatement date, closure date and disposition, together with any database key allowing the NOV data to be linked to the underlying complaint.  Complaints that did not produce an NOV. Produce the complete complaint-data sheet, complaint history/status comments, inspector notes and inspection-history records for complaints involving Similar Conditions at Schedule A Properties during the Detailed Record Period that were closed or disposed of without issuance of an NOV, including complaints reflected as corrected before inspection, no violation observed, unable to verify, unable to gain entry, cancelled, duplicate, withdrawn, referred to another division or agency, or any substantially similar disposition. This request specifically seeks the chronology showing when the complaint was received, when the owner/manager or responsible party was contacted or notified, when inspection occurred, and when the complaint was closed.  Known NOV files identified in the prior Veritas litigation. Produce the complete DBI complaint and code-enforcement file associated with the following complaint/NOV numbers, including complaint data sheets, original complaint narratives, inspection notes, photographs, emails, notices, NOVs, owner/agent responses, permit-history research, reinspections, status histories, referrals, hearing materials and records of abatement or closure: 201707891; 201862011; 201840541; 201718181; 201864231; 201879201; 201872811; 201884363; 201882461; 201860161; 201875001; 201472281; 201875604; 201716591; 201701622; 201711561; 201762202; and 201726391. The Evander pleading specifically identifies these DBI matters across several Veritas-related properties.   Similar-condition underlying files. For each Schedule A Property during the Detailed Record Period, produce complaint narratives, inspector notes, photographs, inspection/reinspection records, NOVs and disposition records for complaints involving Similar Conditions. This request does not seek architectural plans or unrelated permit documents unless they were made part of, referenced in, or relied upon in the complaint/code-enforcement file.  Repeat complaints after purported correction. Produce records sufficient to identify instances during the Detailed Record Period in which a Schedule A Property was the subject of a second or subsequent complaint involving the same or substantially similar condition within 24 months after a prior complaint was closed or an NOV was recorded as abated. Existing database data may be produced instead of manually compiled records if it permits the requester to make that comparison.  Timing and abatement history. To the extent not already produced above, produce existing records sufficient to determine, for each responsive complaint/NOV, the dates of complaint receipt, owner/agent notification or communication, first inspection, subsequent inspection(s), NOV issuance, compliance deadline, claimed correction, verification of correction, referral to Code Enforcement, Director's Hearing, Order/Notice of Abatement and final closure.  Code-enforcement escalation. Produce all Director's Hearing files, staff presentation materials, hearing notices, owner/agent submissions, Notices or Orders of Abatement, assessment-of-cost records, enforcement-fee records, monthly violation-monitoring records, referrals for further enforcement and final dispositions concerning Schedule A Properties during the Detailed Record Period. DBI explains that unabated matters can proceed to Director's Hearings, abatement and further enforcement, and its enforcement records can include inspection, case-management, hearing and referral costs.   City Attorney and other agency referrals. Produce nonprivileged records sufficient to identify every referral during the Detailed Record Period by DBI, HIS, BID or CES to the San Francisco City Attorney or another City enforcement agency concerning a Schedule A Property, including the date of referral, property, complaint/NOV number, subject matter and underlying nonprivileged factual records transmitted with the referral. This request does not seek attorney-client communications or attorney work product.  HRC / VTA / CEOP property records. Produce all DBI-held records created, received or maintained through CEOP or otherwise by DBI during January 1, 2017 through December 31, 2022 that concern HRC/VTA and one or more Schedule A Properties, including referrals, case lists, property lists, complaint lists, liaison records, correspondence, presentations, meeting materials, summaries, spreadsheets and records of communications among HRC/VTA, DBI inspectors and owners/property managers. Tenant names and private contact information may be redacted. DBI identifies CEOP as a formal city/community process through which organizations including HRC act as liaisons between tenants and DBI regarding code compliance.   2018 Board of Supervisors Veritas hearing. Produce all records in DBI's possession relating to San Francisco Board of Supervisors File/Hearing 180436, heard by the Public Safety and Neighborhood Services Committee on May 16, 2018, insofar as the records concern Veritas, Greentree, HRC, the Veritas Tenants Campaign/VTA, construction, habitability, code enforcement or Schedule A Properties. This includes any presentation, slide deck, brief, survey, property list, complaint summary, exhibits or supporting materials received from HRC/VTA; materials prepared by DBI for the hearing; communications concerning DBI's participation; and records of DBI follow-up generated in response to issues raised at the hearing. The City's minutes confirm DBI was requested to report and that HRC, the Veritas Tenants Campaign, Veritas and numerous Greentree representatives participated.   Cross-property or “portfolio” analyses already created by DBI. Produce any existing report, memorandum, spreadsheet, presentation, briefing, dashboard, email attachment or other record created during January 1, 2017 through December 31, 2022 that aggregates, summarizes or compares complaints, NOVs, enforcement activity, unresolved violations or code-compliance issues at more than one Schedule A Property, or otherwise refers collectively to Veritas, Greentree, a “Veritas portfolio,” Veritas-owned properties or Greentree-managed properties. This request does not ask DBI to create a new analysis.  Centralized ownership/management contacts. Produce existing records sufficient to identify any Veritas, Greentree or other common property-management representatives who appeared in DBI complaint or enforcement records for two or more Schedule A Properties, including the name, title/role, business contact information reflected in the public record, properties with which the individual was associated and relevant complaint/NOV numbers. If DBI cannot generate this information without creating a new record, production of the underlying existing owner/agent fields in native electronic form will satisfy this request.  Communications concerning repeated Veritas/Greentree code issues. Produce emails and other written communications from January 1, 2017 through December 31, 2022 maintained by the Chief Housing Inspector, Code Enforcement management, CEOP personnel, or other DBI personnel assigned responsibility for multiple Schedule A Properties that contain “Veritas,” “Greentree,” “RentSFNow,” “Yat-Pang Au,” “Yat Pang Au,” “Veritas Tenant Association,” or “VTA” and also contain any of the following terms or concepts: complaint, code, violation, construction, permit, water, shutoff, mold, lead, asbestos, dust, harassment, habitability, housing service, CEOP, hearing, abatement, City Attorney, or inspection. This request seeks communications addressing property-management/code-compliance matters and not purely administrative communications unrelated to a property or enforcement issue.  Violation Radar. Produce any DBI record from January 1, 2017 through December 31, 2020 communicating with or referring to Violation Radar or Devon Bradley in connection with Greentree, Veritas or a Schedule A Property, including records concerning access to, transmission of, notification concerning, or use of DBI complaint data. If DBI has no responsive records, please state that no records were located. Public reporting stated that Greentree subscribed to Violation Radar beginning in 2017 and that the service alerted property managers to newly filed DBI complaints.   SOL Environmental. Produce all DBI complaint, inspection, permit-related or code-enforcement records from January 1, 2015 through December 31, 2022 for Schedule A Properties that identify or refer to SOL Environmental, including records in which SOL Environmental appears as an environmental consultant, contractor, subcontractor, inspector, investigator, remediation provider or other participant in work involving mold, moisture, lead, asbestos, construction or remediation.  Construction associated with vacant-unit renovation. Produce complaint narratives, inspector comments, inspection records and NOVs during the Detailed Record Period in which a complaint at a Schedule A Property expressly refers to renovation, remodeling or construction in a vacant unit, recently vacated unit, unit being prepared for a new tenant, unit turnover, or substantially similar language. Public Press reported that its review of DBI complaint descriptions found construction complaints increased after Veritas acquisition and frequently concerned renovation of vacant units being prepared for new tenants.   Water/power/service interruption and construction notice. Produce complaint narratives, inspector comments, inspection records and NOVs during the Detailed Record Period concerning planned or unplanned interruption of water, electricity, gas, heat or elevator service at Schedule A Properties where the record also references construction, renovation or repair, including records describing frequency, duration, notice to occupants or absence of notice.  Lead/asbestos containment and unsafe work. Produce complaint narratives, inspector notes, inspection reports, photographs and NOVs at Schedule A Properties during the Detailed Record Period concerning construction dust, lead-paint disturbance, asbestos disturbance, inadequate containment, unsafe demolition or renovation, or alleged work without required permits. Publicly reported DBI complaints from these properties included allegations of unpermitted construction and lack of lead/asbestos containment.   Property-manager/owner responses and early correction. For complaints involving Similar Conditions, produce existing DBI records documenting communications with owners, agents or property managers between receipt of the complaint and the first inspection, including records reflecting that work was performed, a condition was corrected, access was requested, an inspection was cancelled, or the condition was no longer present when DBI inspected.  Files involving long or repeated noncompliance. Produce records sufficient to identify responsive complaints/NOVs at Schedule A Properties for which the condition remained open, outstanding or unverified for more than 30 days after issuance of an NOV, including the subsequent inspection history and eventual disposition. The prior Evander pleading itself alleges numerous specified DBI NOVs remained unabated beyond the stated correction period, making the actual DBI histories particularly important to confirm or disprove that allegation.   Records showing who actually dealt with DBI. For every Schedule A Property, produce existing records sufficient to identify the owner, responsible party, property manager, permit applicant, contractor and/or agent who communicated with DBI concerning responsive complaints, NOVs and enforcement proceedings during the Detailed Record Period. This request seeks the identities reflected in DBI's existing records and does not request that DBI determine legal ownership, agency or corporate affiliation.  Referrals originating with HRC/CEOP. Produce records sufficient to identify complaints or enforcement matters at Schedule A Properties during January 1, 2017 through December 31, 2022 where the complaint, referral or case history indicates that HRC, VTA, CEOP or another CEOP community partner assisted with, communicated about or referred the condition to DBI.  DBI's responses to systemic concerns. Produce any existing memoranda, directives, meeting notes, briefing materials or correspondence during January 1, 2017 through December 31, 2022 in which DBI management discussed whether complaints or construction/code issues involving Veritas or Greentree appeared at multiple properties, whether enhanced monitoring or coordination was warranted, or whether a meeting, outreach effort, referral or other response involving Veritas/Greentree was considered or undertaken.

Subject: California Public Records Act Request — E-Bike, Scooter, and Bicycle Injury Encounter Data (2018–Present)   Hello,   Under the California Public Records Act (Government Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I am requesting aggregate clinical encounter data from all SFDPH-operated facilities — including Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center and all SFHN community health clinics — for patient encounters coded under the ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes described below.   WHAT I AM REQUESTING   These codes fall into three categories: injuries involving standing electric scooters or similar standing micro-mobility devices, injuries involving electric-assisted bicycles, and injuries involving regular (non-motorized) pedal cycles. Rather than requiring you to key in codes by hand, I've described each category by its ICD-10-CM long-description text, then listed the specific codes that match as of the current code set. If your reporting system can query by matching the code's official description text, that's the most reliable way to run this — for example, "any diagnosis code whose long description contains the phrase 'electric (assisted) bicycle,' limited to the 7th-character 'initial encounter' (A) variant."   To avoid any ambiguity, I've also listed the exact codes below that match each phrase as of today (see the full list at the end of this request). Please treat this list as the specification of what I'm requesting — but if your own text-based search turns up additional codes matching these phrases that aren't on my list (for instance, due to a code-description revision in an annual ICD-10-CM update), please include those as well and flag them separately so I know they were added.   I am requesting only the "initial encounter" (7th character "A") variant of each code, which excludes subsequent-encounter and sequela (follow-up) visits for the same injury.   CATEGORY 1: STANDING ELECTRIC SCOOTER / STANDING MICRO-MOBILITY CONVEYANCE  Codes whose ICD-10-CM description contains "standing electric scooter" or "standing micro-mobility pedestrian conveyance" (41 codes; see full list at the end).   CATEGORY 2: ELECTRIC-ASSISTED BICYCLE  Codes whose ICD-10-CM description contains "electric (assisted) bicycle" (79 codes; see full list at the end).   CATEGORY 3: PEDAL CYCLE (REGULAR BICYCLE)  Codes whose ICD-10-CM description contains "pedal cycle," covering the cyclist's own injuries (V10–V19), a pedestrian struck by a cyclist (V01), an electric-assisted bicycle or other motorcycle striking a cyclist (V21), and other vehicle occupants (three-wheeled vehicle, car, pickup/van, heavy truck, bus, animal-drawn vehicle) who struck a cyclist (V31, V41, V51, V61, V71, V80.2) (134 codes; see full list at the end).   Note: 13 codes appear in more than one category above because they describe an incident involving two device types at once (e.g., a scooter rider colliding with a bicycle, or an e-bike colliding with a bicycle). I've left them listed in both places for completeness; please don't double-count them if you're summing totals across categories, since they represent the same underlying encounters.   TIME PERIOD   Please provide data for each calendar year from January 1, 2018 through the most recently completed quarter. I'm aware that these specific ICD-10-CM codes were introduced in the update effective October 1, 2022 (federal fiscal year 2023) and would not have been in use before then — please still run the request across the full 2018–present range, and simply report zero or no responsive records for any year in which the codes were not yet in use. If your system coded similar injuries under different, less specific codes prior to October 2022, you do not need to identify or include those — I'm asking only about the codes listed below, for whatever portion of 2018–present they were actually in effect.   DATA REQUESTED   For each code (or, if easier for your system, aggregated by category and year) and each calendar year in the applicable range, I request:   - Total encounter count  - Total unique patient count (deduplicated across encounters) — please also let me know whether an emergency department visit that resulted in an inpatient admission is counted as one encounter or two in your data, so I can interpret the encounter totals correctly  - Patient sex  - Patient age group  - Place of occurrence, if captured in a structured field (e.g., a Y92-series code or equivalent) — I recognize this may not be reliably captured in clinical records the way it would be in a police collision report, so please provide whatever you have, including "not captured" if that's the case   Given the number of dimensions requested, I recognize some combinations may involve small cell sizes subject to suppression for patient privacy. If that applies, my primary interest is the count of unique patients and encounters broken out by code and year; sex, age group, and place of occurrence are secondary and can be omitted or aggregated further if needed to avoid suppression, so long as the count totals themselves are provided. Please note explicitly wherever a figure has been suppressed or aggregated, rather than omitting it silently.   FORMAT AND SCOPE   I am requesting records in aggregate, de-identified form only — not individual patient records.   Under Government Code § 7922.570, "any agency that has information that constitutes an identifiable public record not exempt from disclosure... that is in an electronic format shall make that information available in an electronic format when requested." I am requesting the data in a machine-readable electronic format (e.g., CSV or Excel, not a scanned image or PDF of a printed table), in whatever electronic format your systems currently hold or produce this data.   Under San Francisco Administrative Code § 67.26, "the work of responding to a public-records request and preparing documents for disclosure shall be considered part of the regular work duties of any city employee, and no fee shall be charged to the requester to cover the personnel costs of responding to a records request." Accordingly, I do not expect to be charged for staff or analyst time to compile or extract this data. Under § 67.28, any duplication fee should not exceed 10 cents per page for custom-assembled records, or one cent per page for routinely distributed documents, plus postage if applicable.   If any portion of this request is denied, please cite the specific statutory exemption(s) relied upon and produce all non-exempt, segregable records.   I am a reporter at the San Francisco Standard, and this request is made in connection with reporting on micro-mobility injuries in San Francisco.   Thank you for your help, and please let me know if you have questions about the code list or need it in a different format. requests.request_text: Records re: Rec & Park inquiry on proposed sport court at Martin Luther King Jr. Pool   Pursuant to the San Francisco Sunshine Ordinance (S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 67) and the California Public Records Act, I request copies of the following records, for the period April 1, 2026 through the date of your search:   1. All communications between DPH (including Corey Chrisman and Environmental Health / recreational water program staff, Douglas Obana, and/or Jennifer Callewaert) and the SF Recreation and Park Department regarding a proposed sport court, tile surface, or resurfacing at Martin Luther King Jr. Pool.  2. All internal DPH communications, notes, code analyses (including CBC Title 24 §§ 3123B and 3140B), and evaluations regarding this proposal.  3. Records showing when DPH received responses to its questions about the proposal (submitted by the applicant on or about July 27, 2026), and any reply, determination, or outstanding question DPH sent to Rec & Park afterward.  4. Any records regarding a draft MoU for the proposal (September 2026).   You may exclude emails on which steven@sfuwh.org was a direct sender or recipient, but please include internal forwards and replies.   Please produce records electronically and on a rolling basis as they become available. If any record or portion is withheld, please cite the specific legal exemption for each and redact rather than withhold entire records.   Thank you,  Steven Tiell  San Francisco Sea Lions Underwater Hockey Club  415-462-0449
